summary: Derived one explicit unconditional Buchstab lower-bound calculation for the original unweighted F_alpha using ordinary BV and the inspected linear-sieve theorem within its actual parameter domain. At fixed alpha in [0.3,1/3), alpha<d<1/2 and beta in [d/4,d/2), the initial lower coefficient is (2/d)log((d-beta)/beta). Switching with the legal weakened cutoff min(r,sqrt(N^d/r)) gives upper coefficient (2/d)log(alpha*(d-beta)/(beta*(d-alpha))); accumulated BV errors have unique-largest-prime moduli. Their difference is exactly (2/d)log((d-alpha)/alpha), independent of beta and at most -4/3 before any semiprime subtraction. A coefficient-uniform two-form sieve supplies an additional nonnegative semiprime upper coefficient, completing an actual but ineffective F minorant. Recorded strict endpoints, q=1 removal, m=1 inclusion, repetitions and prime divisors of N. This is a checkable failure certificate for precisely this one-switch family, not a refutation of Goldbach or all switching methods. Separate review and independent computation are pending; no positive lower margin, breakthrough or novelty claim is made.

claims.text: The exact least-prime partition and parity classification give U_alpha=U_beta-sum C_r and F_alpha=U_alpha-E_alpha, with m=1 and repeated factors retained.
The stated legal linear-sieve calculation has exact pre-semiprime coefficient (2/d)log((d-alpha)/alpha), independent of beta and bounded above by -4/3 on its declared parameter domain.
This particular one-switch minorant cannot certify a positive F lower margin using the chosen classical coefficients; its failure does not imply failure of every switching or double-sieve method.
The actual positive pointwise F margin, Goldbach proof, demonstrated breakthrough and novelty remain unestablished.
